identity.title: Reading between the Rings: Observed Dust Ring Properties as Probes of Planet Masses

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use 2D hydrodynamical simulations of planet-disc interactions to investigate this, focusing on planets ranging $0.5-2.0\times$ the pebble-isolation mass, for three different aspect ratios.

question.value: How do dust ring properties (mass, peak location, width) produced by an embedded planet depend on planet mass relative to the pebble-isolation mass, and can they constrain planet masses in observed discs?

evidence.quote: We hypothesise that dust rings in protoplanetary discs formed by an embedded planet should have properties that reflect the planet’s mass.

findings_qualitative.value: Ring width and mass change with planet mass up to M_iso then plateau; ring peak location is independent of Stokes number

evidence.quote: The dust ring width and mass change with planet mass for planet masses up to the pebble-isolation mass, beyond which they become constant.

claims.hypothesis: Ring peak location scales linearly with planet Hill radius and can give planet mass
claims.experiment: Linear fits to simulated ring peaks; application to PDS 70
claims.result: r_peak=(1.07±0.01)r_p+(5.3±0.3)R_H; PDS 70c 3.3 M_Jup from inner shoulder
claims.finding: Ring peak can estimate planet mass

evidence.quote: We confirm a positive linear relationship between a planet’s Hill radius and the location of a ring’s density peak

claims.hypothesis: Ring width and mass depend on planet mass relative to M_iso
claims.result: Both change below M_iso and plateau above
claims.finding: Rings can distinguish sub- vs super-M_iso planets

evidence.quote: We find the ring’s dust mass, peak location, and width to correlate with planet mass.

claims.hypothesis: Pebble-isolation mass can be defined by pressure gradient asymmetry
claims.experiment: Compared max interior/exterior pressure gradients vs planet mass
claims.result: Interior gradient exceeds exterior above M_iso
claims.finding: New definition of M_iso usable with gas observations

evidence.loc: 4.5 Refining our understanding of pebble-isolation theory
evidence.quote: it is the minimum planet mass which perturbs the gas enough for the pressure gradient interior to the pressure maximum to exceed the pressure gradient exterior to it.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gaussian/Lorentzian ring edge fits rejected due to asymmetric profiles

evidence.quote: Instead, we define our own criteria for identifying the ring edges.

limitations_admitted.value: No migration, dust feedback, dust growth, or 3D; single alpha; circular orbits

evidence.quote: The primary simplification in our models is that all planets are on fixed orbits, unable to migrate.

referee_caveats_inferred: Planet mass scales as cube of ring location offset, giving very large uncertainties
Single alpha=1e-4 and fixed St assumed for aspect-ratio bounds
Scale-free 2D models without growth may not match real rings
